metadata.title: NZ 2026 General Election: party policy scoring matrix and polling inputs
metadata.sources_note: Policy facts are drawn from the per-party research files in research/ (official party policy pages, RNZ, NZ Herald, Newsroom, Stuff, The Spinoff, 1News, Treasury, Ministry of Justice, ERO, Waitangi Tribunal, Wikipedia). Independent-evidence coverage is uneven: National's file is the most complete because the session's web-search quota was exhausted before the other six agents ran; those files rely on official party pages plus Wikipedia. Where the research files lack an independent assessment, the rationale below draws on published evidence known to the author (OECD, Tax Working Group 2019, Productivity Commission, Ministry of Justice evaluations) and says so.
metadata.scoring_methodology: Each party receives an integer 1-10 effectiveness score per domain. The question asked for every score is: based on independent evidence (Treasury, Reserve Bank, OECD, Ministry evaluations, peer-reviewed policy research), how effectively would this party's stated 2026 policies, and its track record where it has governed, advance STABILITY (fiscal and institutional), GROWTH (productivity and output) and EQUALITY (distribution of outcomes) in this domain? Credit is given for evidence-backed, costed, deliverable measures; debits for measures contradicted by evidence, uncosted or unfunded, or carrying material legal or institutional risk. Incumbents (National, ACT, NZ First) are judged partly on delivered outcomes, opposition parties on stated plans; this creates an inherent asymmetry that is flagged as a limitation.
metadata.aggregate_weight: w_i = sum of the 8 domain scores / 80, so w_i is in (0, 1].
metadata.position_axes_note: Separately from effectiveness, each party is placed on a -1..+1 POSITION axis per domain. Positions are not value judgements; they describe where the party's policy sits so that ideological distance between potential coalition partners can be computed. Pairwise friction d_ij = mean over domains of |pos_i - pos_j| / 2, so d_ij is in [0, 1].

position_axes.health: -1 = market/private delivery and spending restraint; +1 = universal publicly funded expansion
position_axes.education: -1 = school choice, charter schools, standardised core; +1 = universal free public provision
position_axes.housing_rental: -1 = landlord/market incentives and tenancy deregulation; +1 = public housing, tenant protection, land/wealth taxation
position_axes.economy_col: -1 = lower tax, smaller government, no new taxes; +1 = new redistributive taxes and larger state
position_axes.employment: -1 = labour-market flexibility and benefit conditionality; +1 = worker protections, higher transfers
position_axes.transport_infra: -1 = roads and fossil-fuel infrastructure priority; +1 = public transport, rail, climate priority
position_axes.tiriti_maori: -1 = single legal standard, wind back Treaty-based arrangements; +1 = Tiriti-based partnership, co-governance, Maori-led institutions

scoring_criteria.health: Funding adequacy and credibility, access (GP, medicines), wait-time outcomes, mental health, preventative care
scoring_criteria.education: Evidence-based literacy/numeracy, infrastructure, teacher workforce, qualification coherence, ECE quality
scoring_criteria.crime_justice: Victimisation and recidivism evidence, rehabilitation, police resourcing, youth justice efficacy, prison cost trajectory
scoring_criteria.housing_rental: Housing supply creation, affordability, tenant security, social housing delivery, planning reform
scoring_criteria.economy_col: Fiscal credibility, inflation and debt trajectory, tax efficiency and equity, grocery competition, growth policy
scoring_criteria.employment: Job creation, real wage growth, worker protections, benefit adequacy and work incentives
scoring_criteria.transport_infra: Project economics (BCRs), institutional reform, public and active transport, emissions, regional connectivity
scoring_criteria.tiriti_maori: Honouring Te Tiriti obligations as found by the Waitangi Tribunal and courts, Maori health/education equity, legal and constitutional risk in either direction

polling_average.method: Unweighted mean of the six most recent national polls retrieved (1News-Verian 23-27 Sep, Post/Freshwater 4-11 Sep, Anacta 4-10 Sep, Taxpayers Union-Curia 1-3 Sep, Roy Morgan 27 Jul-23 Aug, RNZ-Reid Research 14-21 Aug 2026). See research/polling.md.

electorate_assumptions.note: Te Pati Maori is below 5% and enters via Maori electorates; 4 wins is the 1News-Verian September projection and is below the 6 won in 2023 because of the Te Tai Tokerau split and Labour contesting all seven seats. Electorate wins for parties above the threshold do not change their totals unless they exceed the party-vote entitlement, so only Te Pati Maori's count matters for the overhang. ACT's Epsom seat is listed for completeness.

declared_coalition_positions: National (Luxon, Jul and Aug 2026) has ruled out any arrangement with TOP, including confidence and supply, citing TOP's tax policy.
Labour and the Greens announced in February 2026 that they would work together during the campaign and in government (Wikipedia; primary source unverified).
TOP says it will negotiate first with whichever major party wins the most votes, and would not support a government with Winston Peters as foreign minister (Wikipedia; unverified).
NZ First ruled out Labour before the 2023 election; no explicit 2026 rule-out of Labour or Te Pati Maori was found.
National, ACT and NZ First campaign as the incumbent coalition; ACT's slogan is 're-elect the Coalition and help it go further and faster'.
No formal National rule-out of Te Pati Maori, or Labour rule-out of NZ First, was located for 2026; both are widely treated as very unlikely partnerships.

score_rationale.health: All five national health targets improved year-on-year (elective treatment within 4 months 72.6% from 63.9%; ED within 6 hours 76.3%); bowel screening lowered to 56 is modelled to prevent 556 deaths over 25 years; 66 medicines funded from the $604m Pharmac uplift. Against that, Health NZ ran a $722m deficit, unions and the Public Health Communication Centre identify a $300-600m funding gap in Budget 2026, Pharmac's chief executive says the 2026 top-up buys no new medicines, and primary care received no material increase. Delivered improvements, strained funding: 6.
score_rationale.education: Structured literacy, the hour-a-day mandate and phonics checks are strongly evidence-based; 2025 phonics results rose from 26% to 47% at expectation within the year, though only 25% in high-need schools. ERO finds 98% curriculum uptake but only ~60% delivering the full hour. $2.7b school property programme and the new School Property Agency address a documented backlog. The NCEA replacement is coherent but a large transition risk; charter schools have mixed evidence; ECE licensing criteria were cut from 98 to 80, a quality risk. 7.
score_rationale.crime_justice: The NZ Crime and Victims Survey shows violent-crime victims down 27% (136,000) and the lowest victimisation since 2018, with officials cautioning on causation. The sentencing discount cap, Three Strikes and the Gangs Act have weak deterrence evidence and the Ministry of Justice projects the prison population rising 35% to 15,200 by 2036 with Corrections spending reaching $2.4b. The boot-camp pilot saw 7 of 10 reoffend. Better survey outcomes, costly and evidence-poor levers: 5.
score_rationale.housing_rental: Going for Housing Growth is supply-led and evidence-aligned (Auckland upzoning research), but Pillar One slipped to 2027 and no council adopted the MDRS opt-out. The RMA replacement passed in September 2026. Interest deductibility restoration costs ~$800m a year with limited rent effect per Treasury; 90-day no-cause terminations reduce tenant security; Kainga Ora cancelled 60% of 2025 projects. First-home-buyer share hit 29%. 5.
score_rationale.economy_col: No new taxes preserves certainty but leaves NZ's narrow base (no CGT) that the OECD and Tax Working Group criticised. The promised 2026/27 surplus slipped to 2028/29; PREFU 2026 shows a $6.8b deficit, net debt peaking at 43.9% of GDP, Moody's negative outlook and CPI at 4.1% above the RBNZ band. Investment Boost is estimated by Treasury/IR to add 1% to GDP long-run though only 3% of large firms changed plans. The Foodstuffs separation proposal is subject to a ComCom assessment; officials warned in 2023 that forced divestment could carry a $3.8b net cost. Compulsory KiwiSaver is pro-savings. 6.
score_rationale.employment: Minimum wage rises of 1.5-2% trail 4.1% inflation (real decline). Fair Pay Agreements repealed, 90-day trials extended, the Employment Relations Amendment Act 2026 removes unjustified-dismissal rights above $200k, and the Equal Pay Amendment Act 2025 discontinued 33 pay-equity claims ($12.8b saved). MSD evaluation shows 99% compliance with the traffic-light system, but Jobseeker numbers reached 218,000 and the Salvation Army links sanctions to food-parcel demand. Flexibility gains, equity losses: 4.
score_rationale.transport_infra: Roads of National Significance have a $5.1b blowout, most benefit-cost ratios under 2 and Infrastructure Commission process concerns; Mill Road is projected by NZTA to cut deaths and serious injuries 60%. Clean Car Discount repeal cut EV registrations ~70%. The shift to RUC, the National Infrastructure Agency, the 30-year plan and City/Regional Deals are sound institutional reforms. Strong institutions, weak project economics: 5.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Voted down the Treaty Principles Bill, but the Treaty-clauses review proceeds despite the Ministry of Justice finding 'no apparent benefits and significant risks'; Te Aka Whai Ora and section 7AA were repealed and Maori-ward referendums imposed, with Waitangi Tribunal findings of breach. Whanau Ora was recommissioned on a declining baseline. Maori Jobseeker numbers are rising. 3.

key_policies.health: Five health targets to 2030; $5.5-5.8b frontline uplift over four years; 66 medicines funded; bowel screening from 56; 24/7 digital GP service; Waikato medical school
key_policies.education: Structured literacy and maths, hour-a-day, phonics checks; NCEA replaced by NZCE/NZACE from 2028-2030; $2.7b school property; charter schools (with ACT)
key_policies.crime_justice: Sentencing discount cap 40%, Three Strikes reinstated, gang patch ban, military-style academies, 500 extra police, Young Serious Offender declaration
key_policies.housing_rental: Going for Housing Growth, RMA replacement (Planning Bill and Natural Environment Bill), 100% interest deductibility, 90-day no-cause terminations, First Home Loan income cap $300k, Kainga Ora reset
key_policies.economy_col: No new taxes (no CGT or wealth tax), surplus 2028/29, Investment Boost, FamilyBoost, compulsory KiwiSaver 12% by 2032, Foodstuffs separation via ComCom assessment, Electrify NZ 2.0
key_policies.employment: Benefit traffic-light sanctions, moderate minimum-wage rises, FPA repeal, 90-day trials, ERA 2026 $200k dismissal threshold, Equal Pay Amendment Act 2025, paid parental leave to 30 weeks
key_policies.transport_infra: 17 Roads of National Significance ($44-56b), RUC for all vehicles from 2027, National Infrastructure Agency, City/Regional Deals, fast-track consenting, opposes fare cap
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Crown sovereign, needs-not-race targeting; Treaty-clauses review across 19 Acts; Te Aka Whai Ora disestablished; Maori-ward referendums; Whanau Ora recommissioned

score_rationale.health: Medicard (three free GP/nurse visits a year, $553m/yr from 2028) and free prescriptions ($74.5m/yr) target primary-care access, where the evidence base is strongest for reducing ED load and unmet need; the 2023 co-payment removal measurably raised dispensing. An Independent Pricing Authority addresses the 7.6% GP funding shortfall; a graduate nurse job guarantee and $200m hospital repairs are costed, and the package is ring-fenced to CGT revenue. No Pharmac or mental health policy was found. 7.
score_rationale.education: $400m school property and a 10% student-loan write-off are costed, but loan relief is poorly targeted and has weak evidence for access or attainment. Reported plans to pause the NCEA replacement and reverse curriculum settings would add policy churn; school lunch expansion has modest attendance and wellbeing evidence. No position located on structured literacy or teacher pay. 5.
score_rationale.crime_justice: No standalone justice policy on the party site. Reported commitments (corporate homicide offence, repeal of military-style academies) are consistent with the pilot evaluation but thin. 4.
score_rationale.housing_rental: $2.9b to restart Kainga Ora building is supply-positive at the bottom of the market, and a CGT on investment property modestly reduces speculative demand. No tenancy-law, planning or first-home-buyer policy was located, and Labour's 2017-2023 build record was slow. 5.
score_rationale.economy_col: A 28% CGT on investment property from July 2027 moves toward the broad-base system recommended by the Tax Working Group, though its narrow scope limits revenue and creates boundary distortions. The fiscal plan targets OBEGAL surplus in 2028/29 (a stricter measure than OBEGALx) and net debt under 20%; independent economist Cameron Bagrie notes gaps on both sides, and Treasury's $11b pay-equity estimate leaves $8.5b unfunded per National. Wholesale grocery separation matches the Commerce Commission's 2022 wholesale-access recommendation; the three-year fuel-tax freeze costs the land transport fund ~$3.1b. 6.
score_rationale.employment: Pay-equity restoration and a $4/hr rise for 65,000 care workers ($2.5b over four years) directly address a documented gender pay gap, with later settlements unfunded. Apprenticeship Boost expansion has positive completion evaluations; Maori trades training reports 72% employment outcomes. No minimum-wage or Fair Pay Agreement position found. 6.
score_rationale.transport_infra: The $20/$10 weekly fare cap (from July 2027, $91-260m/yr) has evidence from Germany's Deutschlandticket of modest mode shift and strong equity benefit, but the fuel-tax freeze undermines the fund that pays for it. No rail, roads or EV policy located. 5.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Opposes the Treaty Principles Bill and the Treaty-clauses review, funds Maori trades training ($21m/yr) and is reported to reinstate school boards' Treaty obligations. No commitment to re-establish Te Aka Whai Ora or on co-governance was located; cautious partnership stance. 6.

key_policies.health: Medicard: 3 free GP visits/yr from July 2028; free prescriptions from July 2027; Independent Pricing Authority for GP funding; graduate nurse job guarantee; $200m hospital repairs; $15.5b extra health funding
key_policies.education: $400m school property (Start Work Now), 10% student loan cut, reported pause of NCEA abolition, school lunches to 400 more schools
key_policies.crime_justice: No standalone policy; reported corporate homicide offence and repeal of military-style academies
key_policies.housing_rental: $2.9b for Kainga Ora to resume building plus community housing providers; CGT on investment property; SolarSaver
key_policies.economy_col: 28% CGT on investment property from 1 July 2027 ring-fenced to health; OBEGAL surplus 2028/29; net debt <20% GDP; NZ Future Fund; wholesale grocery split; price-gouging ban; 3-year fuel tax freeze; compulsory employer KiwiSaver to 6%
key_policies.employment: Restore pay equity law in 100 days; $4/hr for care workers from Jan 2027; Apprenticeship Boost extension; $1,000 toolbox grants; Maori trades training
key_policies.transport_infra: $20/week public transport cap ($10 outside main centres) from July 2027; fuel tax freeze; Future Fund infrastructure investment
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Oppose Treaty Principles Bill and Treaty-clauses review; Maori trades training $21m/yr; reinstate school boards' Treaty obligations (reported)

Green.full_name: Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand

score_rationale.health: Universal free GP and dental care and free mental health services would close large access gaps (dental is NZ's biggest unmet need), but no costing was found on the policy page and universal dental alone runs to well over $1b a year; funding rests on the wealth tax whose revenue is uncertain. Strong on equity, weaker on fiscal credibility: 6.
score_rationale.education: Universal free ECE has strong evidence for disadvantaged children but is expensive if universal; fees-free tertiary and writing off all student debt (~$16b) is regressive and has weak evidence for participation (Productivity Commission). School lunch expansion has modest evidence. 5.
score_rationale.crime_justice: Restorative justice and community-based youth justice have solid recidivism evidence (Sherman and Strang meta-analyses; Rangatahi Courts), but abolishing life sentences and preventive detention is out of step with public-safety evidence for the highest-risk offenders and has low feasibility. 5.
score_rationale.housing_rental: 40,000 social homes in five years is roughly triple the best historical delivery rate; a 2% annual rent cap is contradicted by the broad economic consensus that rent controls reduce supply and quality over time. Reversing landlord tax cuts is fiscally sound. 4.
score_rationale.economy_col: A 2.5% wealth tax above $10m and a capital-acquisitions tax above $1m aim at equity, but most OECD countries have repealed net wealth taxes over avoidance and valuation problems and the party's own costings needed an $800m correction. KiwiMart (a state supermarket) and forced divestment of 120 stores run against officials' 2023 divestment-cost advice. The $10k tax-free threshold is popular but poorly targeted per the Tax Working Group. 4.
score_rationale.employment: An Income Guarantee, liveable benefits and pay-equity restoration are equity-strong; a shorter working week and default union membership have mixed productivity evidence; costings not found. 5.
score_rationale.transport_infra: Bus lanes, walking and cycling have high benefit-cost ratios and level-crossing removals are safety-justified; $2 fare caps and free fares for large groups have high ongoing cost with modest mode-shift evidence; intercity rail revivals (overnight Auckland-Wellington, Southerner) have weak BCRs in NZ conditions. 6.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Opposes the Treaty-clauses review, funds te reo Maori ($200m), marae and Maori housing energy ($80m), embeds tikanga in marine management; consistent Tiriti-based governance stance aligned with Tribunal findings. 8.

key_policies.health: Universal free GP and dental, free mental health services, pay equity for 65,000 care workers
key_policies.education: Free ECE for all, fees-free tertiary, write off student debt, school lunches to 400 more schools
key_policies.crime_justice: Abolish mandatory minimums, life sentences and preventive detention; replace youth residences and boot camps with community rehabilitation; fund restorative justice
key_policies.housing_rental: 40,000 social homes over five years, 2% rent increase cap, right to housing, Ministry for Green Works, reverse landlord tax cuts
key_policies.economy_col: 2.5% wealth tax above $10m, capital acquisitions tax above $1m, $10k tax-free threshold, 33% rate for largest firms, bank levy, KiwiMart state supermarket, Kiwipower
key_policies.employment: Income Guarantee, liveable benefits, shorter working week, default union membership, restore pay equity
key_policies.transport_infra: Free fares for under-25s and card holders, $2 journey cap, overnight Auckland-Wellington rail, Te Huia to Tauranga, Southerner, bus lanes, level-crossing removals
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Oppose 'stealth Treaty Principles Bill', $200m te reo Maori, marae funding, tikanga in marine law, seabed mining ban

score_rationale.health: Measurable health targets are good governance; expanded pharmacist prescribing has positive UK and Canadian evidence for access. Private-provider expansion can clear waitlists short-term but carries two-tier risk; abolishing the Maori Health Authority removed an equity mechanism. No mental health policy found. 5.
score_rationale.education: Charter schools (18 operating, 1,732 students) have heterogeneous international evidence (CREDO) and only mixed NZ evaluations; no evaluation of the 2025-26 cohort exists yet. Classroom-discipline authority and uniform-cost relief are practical. 5.
score_rationale.crime_justice: Extending Three Strikes to burglary has weak deterrence evidence and adds to the projected 35% prison-population rise; the Arms Act 2026 rewrite implements a long-standing Thorp recommendation. Victim protections positive; no rehabilitation policy. 4.
score_rationale.housing_rental: Opening the building-products market and rewarding councils that consent homes are supply-side measures with Productivity Commission support; interest-deductibility restoration and no-cause terminations shift risk to tenants. 5.
score_rationale.economy_col: Smaller-government and regulatory-discipline agenda supports growth in principle; the Regulatory Standards Act drew 88% opposing submissions and Treasury criticised its 2011 precursor. Scrapping net zero and the carbon price creates trade and transition risk. No tax on KiwiSaver earnings is pro-savings but costly. 5.
score_rationale.employment: Beneficiary medical-certificate requirements, a five-year welfare exclusion for new residents and public-service cuts reduce protections; FPA repeal and 90-day trials delivered. Flexibility without evidence of wage or employment gains: 3.
score_rationale.transport_infra: Policy pages list roads, PPPs and electricity abundance without detail; opposes public-transport subsidy and climate transport measures. 4.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: The Treaty Principles Bill was found by the Waitangi Tribunal to breach the Treaty and by the Ministry of Justice to misstate Article 2, drew ~90% opposing submissions and was defeated 112-11; the party now proposes winding up the Tribunal. High legal and constitutional risk on this axis: 2.

key_policies.health: Measurable targets, private provider expansion, pharmacists do more, Starship for Cancer, closing the medicines gap
key_policies.education: Charter schools expansion, classroom discipline authority, affordable uniforms, rural school buses
key_policies.crime_justice: Three Strikes extended to burglary, Arms Act 2026, deportation of serious offenders, ram-raid prevention
key_policies.housing_rental: Interest deductibility, no-cause terminations, pet bonds, building products liberalisation, reward councils that consent, RMA replacement
key_policies.economy_col: No tax on KiwiSaver earnings, smaller government, scrap net zero and carbon tax, Regulatory Standards Act, supermarket entry
key_policies.employment: Medical certificates for beneficiaries, 5-year welfare exclusion for new residents, FPA repeal, 90-day trials, public service cuts
key_policies.transport_infra: Roads, PPPs, 'Keep NZ Moving', abundant electricity; details not published
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Wind up Waitangi Tribunal, One Law for All, Treaty Principles Bill (defeated 2025), constitutional equal-rights protections

score_rationale.health: 'Make NZ Healthy' emphasises prevention, which is evidence-aligned in principle, but the plan is uncosted and includes clinically contested items (IV vitamin C in surgery, a dietary-guidelines review). No hospital, Pharmac or mental health policy found. 4.
score_rationale.education: No education policy was located beyond reopening the School of Mines and removing student-visa work rights. 3.
score_rationale.crime_justice: The 500 extra police (now delivered late) have good evidence for crime reduction; deportation for any imprisonable offence raises proportionality issues; no rehabilitation or youth-justice policy. 4.
score_rationale.housing_rental: Citizen-first social housing and a Marsden Point special economic zone; immigration restriction can ease demand pressure but there is no supply policy. 3.
score_rationale.economy_col: A 20% company rate below $30m turnover (~$1b/yr) creates threshold distortions the OECD cautions against; a $100b Future Fund, buying BNZ and a $5,000 Kiwi Kids Grant have no identified funding; Paris Agreement withdrawal risks EU and UK FTA clauses. Supermarket and gentailer separation proposals exceed the Electricity Authority's own 2025 review recommendations. 3.
score_rationale.employment: A 20,000 resident-visa cap, 10-year welfare stand-down and citizens-only Super restrict labour supply in shortage sectors and raise legal and equity issues; no wage policy. 3.
score_rationale.transport_infra: The $1.2b Regional Infrastructure Fund has no published evaluation; the Auditor-General and Ombudsman raised concerns about Fast-track executive powers; a $1b oil and gas survey and Paris withdrawal cut against emissions obligations. 4.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Abolishing the Waitangi Tribunal within 100 days, a Maori-seats referendum and disestablishing Auckland's Maori Statutory Board carry high Treaty-breach and litigation risk; did not support the Treaty Principles Bill past first reading. 2.

key_policies.health: Make NZ Healthy prevention plan (15 points, uncosted)
key_policies.education: No published policy; School of Mines; student visa work-rights removal
key_policies.crime_justice: 500 extra police (coalition), deportation for imprisonable offences, 470 corrections officers
key_policies.housing_rental: Citizens-first social housing, Marsden Point special economic zone, fast-track consents
key_policies.economy_col: 20% company tax for SMEs, $100b Future Fund, Foodstuffs break-up and Groceries Commissioner, gentailer split, buy BNZ to merge with Kiwibank, $5,000 Kiwi Kids Grant, Paris withdrawal, $1b oil and gas survey
key_policies.employment: 20,000 resident-visa cap, 10-year welfare stand-down for visa holders, NZ Super citizens-only from 2029, 50% of mining royalties to regions
key_policies.transport_infra: $1.2b Regional Infrastructure Fund, Marsden Point drydock and Northland links, mining and oil and gas, Paris Accord withdrawal
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Abolish Waitangi Tribunal in 100 days, Treaty Completion Commission, Maori-seats referendum, disestablish Auckland Maori Statutory Board, citizens-only voting

score_rationale.health: Re-establishing a Maori-led health authority is supported by the Waitangi Tribunal's Hauora findings and by evidence that by-Maori-for-Maori delivery improved uptake (Covid vaccination). The policy is uncosted and the party has no system-wide health plan. 5.
score_rationale.education: A Maori-led education authority and mataurange Maori integration: Maori-medium students attain NCEA at higher rates than Maori in English-medium schools, supporting the approach; no costings or system-wide policy. 5.
score_rationale.crime_justice: Kaupapa Maori programmes such as Te Pae Oranga show evaluated reoffending reductions (~22%), supporting a Maori-led justice pathway; the stated goal of abolishing prisons by 2040 is not supported by public-safety evidence. 4.
score_rationale.housing_rental: Enabling papakainga on Maori land removes documented barriers; land-banking and vacant-home taxes have modest evidence; no build targets. 5.
score_rationale.economy_col: A 48% rate above $300k, wealth tax and a $1b Energy Sovereignty Fund are equity-oriented; stamp duty is among the least efficient taxes (OECD); no independent costing. 4.
score_rationale.employment: 'Lift incomes' and welfare strengthening without specifics. 4.
score_rationale.transport_infra: Climate resilience and a seabed mining ban; no transport programme. 3.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Te Tiriti Commission, a $200m Matike Mai Fund, UNDRIP implementation and Maori-led authorities are the strongest Tiriti-partnership programme; making Tribunal recommendations binding is a profound constitutional change that scores lower on the stability dimension. 8.

key_policies.health: Rebuild Maori-led health authority, prevention and whanau wellbeing, Maori-led disability services
key_policies.education: Maori-led education authority, matauranga Maori across learning, te reo Maori
key_policies.crime_justice: Maori-led justice authority, reform laws that criminalise poverty, abolish prisons by 2040 (reported)
key_policies.housing_rental: Public and affordable homes, build on Maori land (papakainga), curb land-banking and speculation
key_policies.economy_col: 48% rate above $300k, rebate below $30k, wealth tax, land-banking and vacant-home taxes, stamp duty, $1b Energy Sovereignty Fund, kai sovereignty
key_policies.employment: Lift incomes to live with dignity, strengthen welfare
key_policies.transport_infra: Transport affordability, climate resilience for at-risk communities, seabed mining ban
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Te Tiriti Commission, binding Waitangi Tribunal recommendations, $200m Matike Mai Fund, UNDRIP, constitutional reform by 2040

score_rationale.health: A decade-long cross-party health plan mirrors Danish and OECD recommendations for ending electoral-cycle churn; prevention focus (tobacco, alcohol, food) matches WHO best-buys; lifting spend from 7.4% to 9% of GDP (~$7b/yr) has no identified funding path. Mental health and Pharmac detail absent. 7.
score_rationale.education: An independent Curriculum and Assessment Council and 10-year plan would reduce churn (Estonia, Finland); teacher workload and ECE standards are evidence-aligned; no costings. 6.
score_rationale.crime_justice: Specialist courts (Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Court, Young Adult List, Te Pae Oranga) and sexual-violence court rollout have positive NZ evaluations; post-release case management and employer-linked training are evidence-based reintegration levers. Cannabis regulation has mixed evidence. 7.
score_rationale.housing_rental: A land value tax is regarded by most economists as efficient and hard to avoid; the 2019 Tax Working Group declined to recommend one over liquidity and transition issues, which TOP's deferral provisions partly address. Collapsing 1,000+ zones into 10 national zones and pre-approving prefabs tackle supply constraints with strong evidence; Warmer Kiwi Homes for rentals addresses quality. The most comprehensive supply-and-tax package: 8.
score_rationale.economy_col: The Citizen's Income ($370/wk) removes benefit abatement cliffs and Finnish and Canadian trials show wellbeing gains with neutral employment effects, but the party's own $4b LVT revenue figure is far below the gross cost and no independent costing exists. Commerce Commission structural-separation powers, a lobbying register and an independent costing unit are strong governance measures; R&D to 2% of GDP is OECD-aligned. Innovative but fiscally unverified: 6.
score_rationale.employment: Replacing most benefits with a Citizen's Income improves work incentives in theory; compulsory KiwiSaver 2.0 and employer-linked vocational training are sound; treatment of Super and disability supports unverified. 6.
score_rationale.transport_infra: Legislating the 30-year plan with parliamentary approval to cancel projects over $250m addresses NZ's project-cancellation churn identified by the Infrastructure Commission; 60% of spend on maintenance responds to the OECD ranking NZ last of 33 on upkeep; regulator consolidation and a 30GW renewables target are coherent. The $60b fund relies on borrowing. 7.
score_rationale.tiriti_maori: Honour settlements, restore customary marine title settings, strengthen Treaty analysis in lawmaking, deliberative constitutional conversation and multi-year funding for iwi-led providers; pragmatic partnership without co-governance commitments. 6.

key_policies.health: 10-year cross-party health plan (bottom line), health spend to 9% of GDP, prevention, iwi-led providers with equity goals
key_policies.education: 10-year cross-party education plan, independent Curriculum and Assessment Council, Independent Teaching Council, teacher workload relief
key_policies.crime_justice: Smart on Crime: specialist courts, sexual violence courts, restorative justice, reintegration case management, cannabis regulation
key_policies.housing_rental: 1.75% land value tax (0.5% rural), 10 national planning zones, prefab pre-approval, Warmer Kiwi Homes for rentals, GST refund to councils on new builds
key_policies.economy_col: Tax Reset (LVT plus $370/wk Citizen's Income), ComCom structural separation powers (bottom line), lobbying register and $30k donation cap, R&D to 2% GDP, KiwiSaver 2.0
key_policies.employment: Citizen's Income replaces most benefits, compulsory KiwiSaver rising to 6%, employer-linked vocational training
key_policies.transport_infra: Legislated 30-year infrastructure plan, $60b infrastructure fund, 60% maintenance share, 30GW renewables by 2050, electrify public transport, $5b climate resilience fund
key_policies.tiriti_maori: Honour settlements, restore customary marine title settings, Treaty analysis in lawmaking, constitutional conversation, opposed Treaty Principles Bill
